newsitem.title: MEXICO: Alfa chairman sees strong cash flow.
newsitem.headline: Alfa chairman sees strong cash flow.

text.p: The chairman of Mexican conglomerate Alfa, S.A. said on Thursday that the company expects very strong cash flow for the rest of the year.
"We expect cash generation to remain very strong during the rest of the year," Alfa chairman and chief executive officer Dionisio Garza Medina said in a statement.
He noted that during the first quarter the company "reached record-high levels of EBITDA in dollars for a single quarter notwithstanding reductions in real peso prices resulting from a strong peso."
The company noted that its revenues grew 3.8 percent during the first quarter of this year compared to the fourth quarter of the year before.
In peso terms, revenues fell 2.6 percent, it said.
EBITDA reached $197 million U.S. in the first quarter, an increase of 9.0 percent over the $181 million U.S. reported in the fourth quarter of last year.
In the first quarter interest coverage rose to 5.8 versus 5.0 percent in the last quarter.
Net debt to equity increased slightly to 0.58 from 0.54 in December 1996, Alfa said.
"Capital expenditures in the first quarter were $148 million U.S., representing 21 percent of the budget," it said.
"On the other hand, construction in progress as of the end fo March, 1997 was $343 million U.S.," it said.
